clue.text: Start of melodious song, one from West Side Story

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of melodious
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: The opening of a tuneful number sung by a character in the musical West Side Story.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to think of the song 'Maria' itself; here the character is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story, in love with Tony.

clue.text: This poem unsettled the devil

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem that disturbed the devil himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephisto, short for Mephistopheles, is the devil of the Faust legend, itself told in Goethe's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto is a short form of Mephistopheles, the demon to whom Faust sells his soul.

clue.text: Approach ladder ahead

blocks.note: a ladder in a stocking is also called a run
up means ahead, as in a team being up

explanation.surface: Heading towards a ladder placed in front.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach to something, like the period before an event or an athlete's approach to a jump.

clue.text: No cowboy films in the pipeline? Here's one about war

annotation.answer: ALL QUIET ON THE WESTERN FRONT

definitions.text: No cowboy films in the pipeline?

blocks.clueFragment: No cowboy films in the pipeline?
blocks.note: cryptic meaning: nothing stirring on the front where westerns are made
plain meaning: a famous novel and film about the First World War

explanation.surface: No new westerns are coming soon, but here's a war story instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is read as a news report on the western genre: nothing happening on the 'western' front.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarque's novel, filmed several times, describes German soldiers in the trenches of the First World War.

clue.text: What could make row? Estate car, maybe

indicators.note: asks what these letters could be made into, inviting a rearrangement

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle question: what could cause an argument? Perhaps the family estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate car' reads as one phrase, but 'Estate' belongs to the letters and 'car, maybe' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater is a vehicle with room for only two people, typically a small sports car, so a car is one example.

clue.text: See 3
One can't really see it being a trick

definitions.text: One can't really see it being a trick

blocks.note: surface reading: something invisible or hard to make out
setter's reading: something seen that is not really there, a trick of the eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't really see it' sounds like poor eyesight; it means what is seen isn't real.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is an image that deceives the eye into seeing something that is not truly there.

clue.text: PM from East End, surprisingly

indicators.note: something surprising turns out differently from expected, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for East
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister who unexpectedly came from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class district of London, an unlikely home for a Tory PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony Eden was the British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Martial art dan we took out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are wrong or disordered, so they are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A martial art in which we took a black-belt grade.
explanation.walkthrough: A dan is a grade of black belt in martial arts, which makes the surface fit neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae kwon do is a Korean martial art known for its high kicks.

clue.text: This helps one to see girl after note's written

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's name is written after a musical note, which helps someone read it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl after note' means the name comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that makes vision possible.

clue.text: Order soldiers to board plane abroad, heading for terrible place housing convicts

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order
the heading of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to settle is to put in order or resolve
soldiers are men of the ranks
first letter of terrible

explanation.surface: Instructions to get troops onto an aircraft overseas, bound for some dreadful destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces join in a different order from the clue: the rearranged word comes first. Australia's Botany Bay was the classic British penal settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal settlement was a colony where transported criminals were kept and made to work.

clue.text: An unwise act giving cheek about king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: cheek is insolence, impudence
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone does something foolish by being rude to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' in the British sense is rudeness, not part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence can mean a rash or ill-judged deed, as well as the quality of being unwise.

clue.text: Small pale bird

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A description of a little, washed-out bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan is a large, long-necked white water bird.

clue.text: Not appointed, girl's cross with editor

blocks.note: Una's: the possessive of the girl's name Una
a cross is a sign, as in a mark made instead of a signature
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: An unchosen girl is angry with the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is a noun, a mark or sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassigned means not allocated or given a post, as in not appointed to a role.

clue.text: Soldiers diving into English river in flood

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: a river in flood is a torrent

indicators.note: diving into puts one thing inside another, so the first goes within the second

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers
the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Troops plunge into a swollen English river.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is a stock crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent rush of water, as a river becomes when swollen.

clue.text: Resolve to put out US president

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or displaced, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A determination to oust an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Some poplin in gaberdine for padding

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found across popLIN IN Gaberdine

explanation.surface: A tailor uses a bit of one fabric inside a gaberdine coat as stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplin and gaberdine are both fabrics, which makes the hidden word fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A lining is a layer of material sewn inside a garment, which can serve as padding.

clue.text: Remains with Scottish banker on board express

blocks.note: a banker is something with banks, a river; the Tay is in Scotland
on board means inside a steamship, SS, whose letters wrap what goes aboard
to put something is to express it in words

explanation.surface: Something remains with a Scottish bank official aboard an express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, and 'on board' conventionally means inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays put means remains in the same place without moving.

clue.text: Paint firm to left of us

blocks.note: CO is short for company
L is the abbreviation for left
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A decorating company positioned on our left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour something is to paint or tint it, and colour also means a pigment or paint.

clue.text: Manage to survive in US city, on beer?

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Getting by in an American city on nothing but beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure through a hard period to its end, which is surviving it.

clue.text: Fibre shown in service by one based in Florida

indicators.note: something based in a place sits inside it

blocks.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is an armed service
outer letters of Florida
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fibre is displayed at an air force base in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: the I goes inside the outer letters of Florida, F(I)A, after RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is fibre from the leaves of a palm, used for weaving baskets and mats.

clue.text: Primate's cross and crown

blocks.note: an ape is a primate; the 's means it has what follows
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A monkey owns a crucifix and a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the top or highest point, as the crown is the top of the head.

clue.text: Very loud American I've accommodated in Ely, lavishly

indicators.note: something accommodated in a place is housed within it

blocks.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
US is the abbreviation for American
taken as written
taken as written; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A noisy American has been put up in the city of Ely in grand style.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; FF is the musical marking fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusively means with gushing, unrestrained warmth, so it can stand for lavishly, as in praise.

clue.text: Run away with girl after writer is ditched

indicators.note: something ditched is thrown away, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Penelope is a girl's name
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A girl runs off with someone once the author is dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away with' reads as one phrase, but only 'Run away' defines; PENELOPE loses PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly in order to marry.

clue.text: Caught in South Africa with millions from dishonest scheme

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside something else

blocks.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed in South Africa with millions taken from a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' does double duty: C, and the signal to put it inside SA: S(C)A, then M.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or fraud, a dishonest scheme to cheat people.

clue.text: A starter, perhaps - phone cousin for mixture around noon

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon; around means it joins the letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to ring a relative about lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but its letters join the jumble. 'Starter' is the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: French onion soup is a classic first course, and a starter is the dish that opens a meal.

clue.text: Robot making car chap's getting round to

indicators.note: getting round something means enclosing it on all sides

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile
a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A robot building cars while a worker is busy getting round to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making car' suggests a factory robot, but 'making' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, a robot.

clue.text: Lived with flipping obscene transvestite initially

indicators.note: flipping turns something over, so the word is read from end to start
initially points at the first letter only

blocks.note: lewd means obscene
first letter of transvestite

explanation.surface: Someone lived alongside a very rude cross-dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear-word adjective, but it reverses the word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to reside or live somewhere.
